items.title: fleet search: add the backup verb (atlas-backup port, #14129)
items.body: Refs #14129 (slice of #5670 §8) — the backup verb lands; the issue stays open for the unit switch-over, one nightly cycle on the fleet path, retiring the outside copies, and the #5670 update. ## What this is `fleet search backup` — a faithful port of the live `atlas-backup` shell routine (`nixos/home/atlas-backup.sh`) into the fleet binary: - snapshots the canonical local atlas.db consistently (`sqlite3 .backup`), gzips deterministically (mtime 0, no stored name), files the **same bytes** to the laptop backups root, R2 (`supabase-backups` / `atlas//…`), and Google Drive (`Cloud/cold-store/db-backups/local-atlas/`) - sha256-verified at every destination; the shell original's manifest shape, dedupe against `backup-log.md`, rotation (newest 7 dates laptop + R2, newest 4 archives on Drive), verdict/log line formats, and exit codes are unchanged, so the systemd unit and anything scraping them keep the same contract - R2 credentials from Bitwarden Secrets Manager at runtime, by key name only, never logged; the Drive leg uses the laptop's existing rclone `drive` remote Deliberate differences, all mechanical (also recorded in the module docs): the probe (integrity check, row counts, hashes, manifest) runs in-process instead of through the shell original's embedded Python step, so the verb needs `sqlite3`/`rclone`/`bws` but not `python3`; gzip bytes come from flate2, so the first verb run's archive hash differs from the shell original's even for an unchanged DB (one non-deduped upload, then dedupe is self-consistent); paths/tools accept `ATLAS_BACKUP_*` env overrides (defaults = the shell original's values) so the contract test can run the verb against stub tools. Also in this PR: the fleet-registry search inventory gains `backup`, and the Fleet Book's search reference documents the verb. ## Premise evidence (from #14129) - Copy reconciliation (recorded by the prior lane, comment 7123982770): the nix copy is the live one; `~/tmp/atlas-backup.sh` is gone; the hatch-personal Python copy is the outside copy to retire once the unit switches. - The timer run the prior park waited to observe has now happened — and failed like the one before: `atlas-backup.service` started 2026-11-24 04:58:20 CST, killed 06:28:20 CST, `Result: timeout` (identical to 2026-11-23). The shell backup times out nightly; the verb is the fix path. ## Verification Route: laptop worktree off the existing clone (named fallback — CI runs on main only; a fleet Actions exec session was started but its runner cannot reach this repo's branch, the recorded no-cross-repo-credentials gap, so it was closed unused). - `cargo test -p fleet-search` — 30 lib tests + 2 doc/other suites, all pass; includes the new backup unit tests (MD5 vs the RFC 1321 vectors, calendar validation, dedupe-log parsing per the shell rule, deterministic-gzip header) and `tests/backup_contract.rs`: the verb end-to-end against stub `sqlite3`/`bws`/`rclone`, asserting identical sha256 at all three destinations, the manifest fields, the OK/UNCHANGED verdicts and log lines, and rotation to the newest 7 laptop dates. The contract oracle is the shell script's documented behaviour. - `cargo test -p fleet-registry` — pass. - `cargo check -p fleet --features search,search-serve` — pass. - `cargo fmt --check` on the touched crates — clean. ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-25T06:53:28Z", "session_id": null, "lane": null, "host": "htch-runtime", "worktree": null, "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": null, "auth_subject": "archer", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(atlas-search): vendor Python reference and v3 golden set
items.body: Part of #5670. ## Summary ```text pkgs/atlas-search/ ├── atlas_search.py ├── eval/ │ ├── eval3.py │ ├── README.md │ └── fixtures/golden-311.json └── fixtures/ ├── gen_core_fixtures.py -> ../atlas_search.py └── core-expectations.json (refreshed against the current reference) ``` The fixture generator now loads the checked-in reference instead of the laptop home-directory copy. The eval docs retain source hashes and distinguish the corpus-specific runner from the generic Rust `atlas-eval` scorer. ## Evidence - `~/atlas/v3-venv/bin/python -I pkgs/atlas-search/fixtures/gen_core_fixtures.py` — pass. - `python3 -I -m py_compile pkgs/atlas-search/atlas_search.py pkgs/atlas-search/eval/eval3.py pkgs/atlas-search/fixtures/gen_core_fixtures.py` — pass. - Source and repository `eval3.py` runs on the frozen corpus produced identical summary and all 311 rank records (corpus fingerprint verified; recall@10 142, MRR 0.2655). - `cargo test -p atlas-core` — pass: 42 unit, 5 parity, 11 shard, and 6 stage tests. - `cargo run -p atlas-core --bin atlas-eval -- fixtures/eval-smoke.json test` — pass. The smoke fixture is synthetic and is not evaluation evidence. ## Merge Danger **Door:** Two-way **Blast Radius:** Atlas search reference/evaluation tooling only; no runtime service behavior changes. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added a command-line tool for hybrid full-text and vector search across Turso or local SQLite, with filters for content type, topic, project, client, date, and sensitivity. - Search results can include grouped sessions, nearby chunks, parent messages, or readable text. A separate command retrieves chunk and session details. - Added an evaluator for comparing full-text, vector, and hybrid search against a frozen query set. - **Documentation** - Documented the evaluation datasets, reference tools, and how to run the baseline.

items.title: fix(mcpx): name both daemon digests, shape-derived cache version, status never starts a daemon (#1866)
items.body: Implements the three #1866 fixes from triage task 2758 (queue task 3085): 1. **Two digests, one name** — the daemon info file's `configHash` held the schema-cache digest while `/v1/resolve`'s `configHash` is the daemon key. `Info` now writes `schemaHash` (server-definition digest, `Registry.ConfigHash()`) and `daemonKey` (`FingerprintConfig` over the config sources) as distinct fields. In-repo readers verified: the resolver and the opencode plugin both take the key from the info file's *name*, never the field; the plugin's `DaemonInfo` type is updated to match. `/v1/resolve` is unchanged in meaning. 2. **Schema-cache versioning** — `cacheVersion` is no longer a hand-bumped integer. It is derived at startup from the JSON shape of `cachedEntry` and every struct type reachable from it (`shape-`), so a cache file written by a differently-shaped build fails the version check in `loadCache` and is invalidated instead of silently serving empty fields. Regression test `TestLoadCacheIgnoresStaleShapeFiles` reproduces the Annotations case byte-for-byte (legacy numeric `version: 6` file with an annotations-bearing tool is not seeded), plus a foreign-shape string version. 3. **`mcpx status` autostart** — the non-starting decision is now documented in `mcpx status` help (manual `Detail`, verified in `mcpx help status` output) and in the docs/story.md command table. Tests (laptop, pkgs/mcpx): - Targeted daemon tests pass, incl. the two new tests (`TestLoadCacheIgnoresStaleShapeFiles`, `TestInfoFileNamesBothDigests`) and all resolve/hash tests; `internal/cli` package passes; plugin `daemon.test.ts` 21/21. - Full `go test ./...`: every package passes except `internal/daemon`'s full-package run, which dies with `signal: terminated` in the takeover tests — reproduced identically on a clean origin/main worktree tonight, i.e. pre-existing/environmental, not from this change (the same tests pass in isolation in both trees). Cross-repo check: dezren39/nix carries no mcpx daemon source (only `mcpx.config.nix`, planning docs, and a nixbuild workflow), so no port is owed there. Merge note: this PR is merge-ready pending CI/Codex, but the merge queue is stalled repo-wide (#2403); it should be enqueued once #2403 is fixed. Queue task 3085 is parked on that gate. Refs #1866 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Clarified that `mcpx status` does not start a daemon. If none is running, it reports that status and exits; use `mcpx serve` or a command that requires a daemon to start one. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved schema cache version checks so stale or incompatible cache files are ignored rather than used.
